title: Broad except Exception/BaseException around a body that may hide real faults
purpose: Prevent over-broad handlers that convert every programming error and unexpected failure into one indistinguishable default, making real faults silent.
trigger: An except clause names the broad class Exception or BaseException (the engine already flags the barest 'except:' separately). Such a catch almost never matches an individually-justifiable failure class.
correct: Catch the narrowest exception class the operation can raise for the reason you intend; provide distinctly-typed raises/returns; never swallow. When context is needed on a genuine failure, re-raise with 'raise ... from exc'.
compiler_relationship: Advisory best-practice rule; legal Python, but broad catches routinely hide bugs an authoring LLM introduced.
return_semantics: A LanguageRulePage may be opened and then returned to the originating cycle.
